To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feeding a zinc amino acid complex with zinc sulfate increased colostrum immunoglobulin G concentration, decreased prepartum DMI, increased postpartum DMI and MY, and decreased services per conception.

supplementing zinc as Availa-Zinc (a mixture of zinc amino acid complexes and zinc sulfate) in place of only zinc sulfate increases colostrum immunoglobulin G concentration, decreases days to first service, and linearly improves milk yield per kilogram of dry matter intake in dairy cows.
the ratio of zinc from amino acid complex to inorganic sources in the diets of dairy cows is an important determinant of production responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
evaluating the effect of feeding zinc amino acid complex on the performance of dairy cattle.
the effects of dietary zinc on the performance of dairy cows.
the use of Zn in dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

supplementing zinc as Availa-Zinc (CZ) and zinc sulfate (ZS), as opposed to only ZS, has a beneficial impact on production parameters in Holstein cows, with these benefits becoming more apparent at increasing ratios of CZ to ZS.

feeding CZ as a mixture of zinc sulfate and CZ to pre- and post-partum Holstein cows increases milk production and feed efficiency, decreases milk fat concentration and milk urea nitrogen, decreases services per conception and increases colostrum immunoglobulin G.
supplementing zinc as zinc amino acid complex in addition to zinc sulfate, as compared to supplementing zinc sulfate alone, improves performance in dairy cows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

feeding CZ as a replacement for zinc sulfate in the diet of dairy cows improves colostrum quality and feed efficiency, and may decrease milk fat concentration and increase milk urea nitrogen concentrations.

supplementing 75 mg of Zn/kg of dietary DM as a 40:60 ratio of CZ to Zn sulfate increased milk yield, milk fat-corrected milk, milk protein yield, and solids-cored milk yield, whereas feeding a 16:84 ratio of CZ to Znsulfate decreased milk fat concentration.
supplementing zinc as CZ and zinc sulfate is a more effective means to improve performance of dairy cows relative to supplementing only with zinc sulfate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feeding zinc as a mixture, as opposed to feeding zinc sulfate alone, has beneficial effects in lactating dairy cows.
feeding zinc in a complex form (CZ) can be beneficial to dairy cows.
feeding a mixture of CZ to zinc is beneficial to dairy cows, and feeding more CZ to zinc sulfate is better than feeding less.
